drawings.notes: Step (i) of the invention's own route, drawn immediately under the (i) text. One left-to-right arrow. The only text on the arrow is 'Oxidant / RuO2' printed ABOVE it, with the 2 as a subscript; there is nothing whatever printed below the arrow, and the band under it is blank. Ring positions were read off the drawn hexagons and not inferred: both rings are drawn vertex-up, the top vertex carries CH3 (left structure) or the COOH drawn as O= and OH (right structure), the upper-right vertex carries NO2, and the bottom vertex, para to the top one, carries the SO2 whose H3C is written to its lower left. Labels read 'Formula IV' and 'Formula III', both checked at 6x because degraded ink makes III and IV easy to confuse. The preceding bracketing marker is on p06 and is not visible on this page, so it is recorded as null rather than guessed. Every stroke in this drawing is broken dotted ink because the publication lost its greyscale (brief section 9), so the reaction arrow looks dashed on the page. Read at 4x to 6x magnification it is a degraded solid line with one solid filled arrowhead, and it is recorded as solid.

drawings.notes: Step (ii) of the invention's own route, drawn immediately under the (ii) text. Two reactants joined by a printed plus sign, then one left-to-right arrow. The arrow carries NO text at all: nothing above it and nothing below it, both bands checked blank at 4x. The dione ring is drawn vertex-up with =O on the top vertex and =O on the lower-left vertex, meta to it, read off the drawing; it carries no 'Formula' label of its own. In the product, the benzene is drawn rotated so that the ester carbonyl leaves the upper-right vertex (C1), NO2 is on the top vertex (C2) and the SO2CH3 is on the lower-left vertex (C4). In the product's second ring the ester O attaches to a ring carbon whose ring double bond runs to the carbon adjacent to the ketone carbon, so the ketone is three positions round from the enol carbon; only the two structures either side of it made this ring readable, and the double bond was confirmed as two parallel lines at 5x. Every stroke in this drawing is broken dotted ink because the publication lost its greyscale (brief section 9), so the reaction arrow looks dashed on the page. Read at 4x to 6x magnification it is a degraded solid line with one solid filled arrowhead, and it is recorded as solid.

drawings.notes: Step (iii) of the invention's own route, drawn immediately under the (iii) text. One left-to-right arrow carrying NO text at all: nothing above it and nothing below it, both bands checked blank at 5x. This is the rearrangement, and the drawn product is an isomer of the drawn reactant: the ester O is gone, the aroyl carbon is bonded directly to the ring carbon that sits between the two ketones, and both ring ketones are drawn as separate C=O with no ring C=C left. In the product the benzene is drawn with the aroyl carbon leaving the upper-right vertex (C1), NO2 on the top vertex (C2) and SO2CH3 on the lower-left vertex (C4); its sulfone is drawn with the S on the bond and 'O2' set below the S rather than as one 'SO2' label, which was checked at 5x. Labels read 'Formula II' and 'Formula I', both checked at 6x. Every stroke in this drawing is broken dotted ink because the publication lost its greyscale (brief section 9), so the reaction arrow looks dashed on the page. Read at 4x to 6x magnification it is a degraded solid line with one solid filled arrowhead, and it is recorded as solid.

discrepancies.what: Step (i) names the catalyst and the oxidant class in prose, and the drawing labels the same arrow the same way, but neither names the oxidant itself; the oxidant is written but never identified on this page.
discrepancies.drawing_says: the arrow of the first scheme carries only 'Oxidant / RuO2' above it
discrepancies.text_says: 'with an oxidant in presence of ruthenium (IV) oxide (RuO2) as a catalyst', which also leaves the oxidant unnamed

discrepancies.what: Step (ii) prose names the second reactant, but the second scheme draws that reactant without any label, and draws no reagent, solvent or condition on its arrow.
discrepancies.drawing_says: the second scheme's arrow carries no text above or below it, and its middle structure carries no printed label
discrepancies.text_says: 'reacting NMSBA of formula (III) with 1, 3-cyclohexanedione to produce an enol ester of formula (II)'

discrepancies.what: Step (iii) prose says the enol ester is converted to mesotrione but names no reagent or condition, and the third scheme's arrow is likewise bare, so nothing on this page says how the rearrangement is effected.
discrepancies.drawing_says: the third scheme's arrow carries no text above or below it
